description: A diagnostic adapter for Self-EvolveRec that measures a trained recommender through a stable compatibility interface and generates an interpretation prompt grounded in measured metrics and their definitions.
motivation: Support diagnosis-driven model improvements while preserving fair comparison across four Amazon datasets and avoiding assumptions about unavailable reviews, item attributes, or simulator traits.
implementation_notes: Retain DiagnosisProbe(view, device), run_full_diagnosis(train_loader), and diagnosis_interpreter_prompt(raw_diagnosis). Access the trained network through view.model and adapt architecture-specific probes while preserving the supplied compatibility contract. Training batches contain sequence, positive, and negative tensors of shape B × L. Use only public histories, titles, descriptions, and timestamps. Supply full-catalog unseen-item recommendations to 20 real training users, five per category. Select models using macro-average validation HR@10 across all four categories under the pinned evaluator; exclude hidden test data.
pseudocode:
class DiagnosisProbe(view, device):
    run_full_diagnosis(train_loader):
        preserve model training state
        put view.model in evaluation mode
        disable gradients
        measure supported diagnostics from batches and available public data
        restore model training state
        return {metrics: measured_values, metric_definitions: definitions}

function diagnosis_interpreter_prompt(raw_diagnosis):
    include measured metrics and their definitions
    identify unavailable information explicitly
    request evidence-grounded interpretation and improvement hypotheses
    return prompt

For each candidate:
    train using the prescribed splits and seeds
    run adapted diagnostics
    generate full-catalog unseen-item recommendations for designated users
    select using common macro validation HR@10

originality.positive: Combines a stable diagnostic interface with explicit evidence constraints and a shared evaluation objective.
originality.negative: The description defines an integration contract rather than a new recommendation algorithm or diagnostic method.

future_potential.positive: Could support consistent diagnosis and iterative improvements across multiple recommender architectures.
future_potential.negative: Usefulness depends on the quality of the implemented probes and whether their findings translate into validation gains.

code_difficulty.positive: The required interface and batch format are explicit, making a baseline adapter straightforward.
code_difficulty.negative: Architecture changes require careful probe adaptation, correct model-state handling, and consistent training and inference implementations.
